title: Meet Tannat
subtitle: A grape named for its grip
objectives: Describe Tannat's colour, tannin and flavours

steps.title: Dark and grippy
steps.body: Tannat is a black grape from south-west France, near the Pyrenees. Its name likely comes from the same root as tannin, and it has more than almost any other grape. In the glass it is deep purple, almost black, with blackberry, plum, liquorice and smoky, spicy notes. Acidity is high too.
steps.highlight: Very high tannin, very dark colour

steps.title: Why so tannic
steps.body: Tannat has small berries with thick skins, and unusually many seeds: often five per berry, where most grapes have two to three. Skins and seeds both carry tannin. Tannat is also very rich in procyanidins, a family of antioxidant compounds, and studies have found it among the highest of all red grapes.

steps.prompt: Why does Tannat have so much tannin?
options: Its berries have thick skins and many seeds
It is blended with white grapes
steps.explanation: Tannin comes from skins and seeds. Tannat has thick skins and often five seeds per berry.

steps.title: Spotting it
steps.body: A young Tannat is almost opaque, with a purple rim. On the palate, the tannin grips the gums firmly, more than Cabernet Sauvignon. The fruit is dark, the finish often slightly bitter and spicy. With a few years in bottle, the tannins soften and leather and tobacco notes appear.

steps.prompt: A young Tannat usually has more tannin than a young Cabernet Sauvignon.
steps.explanation: Yes. Tannat is one of the most tannic grapes in the world, firmer than most Cabernet.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Tannat is very dark and very tannic, with high acidity
Thick skins and many seeds give it that grip
It shows blackberry, liquorice and smoke, softening with age
